title: Differences, % changes, log returns — and spreads

explain.prompt: In 4–6 sentences: why do daily log returns of Brent add up exactly to the total move while daily % changes do not? Why does `make_returns` refuse WTI and the Brent–Dubai spread, and what do you use instead? Why must missing days be dropped before computing returns?
rubric: log(P_T / P_0) = Σ log(P_t / P_{t−1}): log returns are additive over time — here they sum to 0.357, exactly log(78.58 / 55.00). % changes compound: their plain sum (0.444) is not the total return (+42.9 %).
For small moves log returns and % changes are close (log(1 + r) ≈ r): % changes for communication, log returns for statistics and aggregation.
WTI printed −35.90 and the Brent–Dubai spread is sometimes negative: a log (or a % change on a near-zero base) is undefined. Use differences in USD/bbl (diff) for these series.
The −35.90 print makes WTI's daily change −47.5 then +46.1 USD/bbl: differences remain defined, but they are dominated by the event — handle it explicitly in any statistic.
Returns are measured between consecutive observed prices; with holiday NaNs left in, diff() produces NaN on the holiday and on the next day, so the move across each holiday disappears from the data.
